assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy link basic hormone biology (proglucagon processing, the insulinotropic action of GLP-1) to drugs that now transform treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and very large, lasting clinical impact are all strong.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and metabolism of GLP-1), Drucker (biology of GLP-1/GLP-2 and its receptor signalling) and Knudsen (design of the acylated, long-acting analogues liraglutide and semaglutide) cover discovery, mechanism and translation. Mojsov's contribution to GLP-1 identification and the roles of others not on the list (for example Habener) are contested and cannot all be accommodated within three names.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed independently over decades and by large outcome trials; recognition is timely given the global clinical effect and ongoing expansion of indications.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit for the original identification of the active GLP-1 peptide is disputed.
Choosing three from four credited names leaves a notable contributor out.
I am relying on my own recollection of the history, not independently verified facts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering patient T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living drugs. The concept, proof of principle and clinical delivery are clear and of lasting importance.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation and CD19/4-1BB CAR-T in leukaemia), Sadelain (CD28 costimulated CAR design and preclinical foundation) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early clinical CAR work) form a plausible trio. Early CAR conception by Eshhar and others is not among the credited names, which weakens a complete assignment.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and multi-year follow-up show durable benefit in blood cancers; efficacy in solid tumours and toxicity management remain unresolved, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: The foundational chimeric-receptor concept predates the credited names and may require recognition.
Whether Rosenberg is the right third laureate rather than another contributor is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational targeting of the BCR-ABL kinase with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukaemia from a fatal disease into a manageable one and established the paradigm of oncogene-directed therapy. The impact on both cancer biology and clinical practice is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery programme), Druker (clinical development and demonstration of efficacy) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) is a coherent configuration. Upstream work on the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL, by others not credited here, is part of the history.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of follow-up and extensive independent confirmation; the paradigm is fully established. Recognition is arguably overdue, which is a mild concern only because the Lasker award already acknowledged it.
uncertainties: Precedence relative to the earlier chromosomal and oncogene discoveries.
Industry versus academic credit division between Lydon and the others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type specific control of activity with millisecond precision, and has reshaped circuit dissection across model systems. The tool is original, broadly adopted and enabling for countless discoveries.
assessment.attribution: Hegemann and Nagel (and Bamberg) identified and characterised channelrhodopsin; Deisseroth and Boyden demonstrated neuronal control; Miesenböck proposed and tested genetically targeted photostimulation earlier. With up to three names the allocation is genuinely contested and any trio omits major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Technique is thoroughly validated and widely used; therapeutic use (vision restoration) is early, but the research impact is already mature.
uncertainties: Six credited names for a three-person limit; priority disputes between the early demonstrations of neuronal control.
Whether a methods advance is judged as a discovery in physiology or medicine.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explained how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies, cancer immunity and senescence. A clear and original mechanistic discovery with wide conceptual reach.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and its product cGAMP, the decisive biochemical step; Barber identified STING as the adaptor. Ishikawa shares credit for the STING discovery and Sun and Wu were first authors on the cGAS work, so the allocation is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been broadly confirmed and extended; therapeutic translation is still at an early stage, so clinical impact is not yet shown.
uncertainties: Credit for STING between Barber and Ishikawa is uncertain.
Therapeutic validation is not yet established.
Reliance on my own recollection of the literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phase separation as an organising principle of the cell (P granules, nucleoli, stress granules) changed how cellular compartments without membranes are understood, with connections to neurodegeneration and cancer. The concept is original and highly influential.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman demonstrated liquid-like behaviour of P granules and set the framework; Görlich and McKnight contributed related work on FG repeats and low-complexity domains. A two-person configuration is defensible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Strong conceptual momentum, but the physiological relevance of many condensates, and the evidence for specific disease mechanisms, remain debated; recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Controversy over how generally condensates are functional rather than artefacts of overexpression or in vitro assays.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing long-term self-renewing three-dimensional organoids from single adult Lgr5-positive stem cells created a widely used platform for tissue biology, disease modelling and personalised medicine research. Original and with rapidly growing impact.
assessment.attribution: Clevers identified Lgr5 stem cells and led the organoid development, with Sato as first author of the key Nature papers. Clevers is the clear central figure; Sato's inclusion is reasonable but secondary.
assessment.maturity: Methods are reproduced worldwide; clinical use is emerging. Reasonably mature as a research tool, but patient benefit is still limited.
uncertainties: Whether the Nobel committee would regard a platform technology as a discovery.
Sato's role relative to other group members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new form of intracellular signalling from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, with consequences for secretory physiology, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. A classic, clearly defined mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently deciphered the pathway (Ire1, Hac1/XBP1 splicing, signalling to the nucleus), making a two-person assignment natural. Other contributors such as Kaufman and Ron could be considered but are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and conceptual stability; ongoing translation (ISRIB, targeting of the integrated stress response) is early. Recognition would be timely or even overdue.
uncertainties: Omitted contributors to the PERK and ATF6 arms of the response.
